ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Smoking cessation

A man taking a stable theophylline dose stops smoking during hospitalization. No dose adjustment is made. Several days later he develops nausea and tachycardia with an elevated drug concentration. Which change best explains the increased exposure?

  1. Reduced intestinal absorption
  2. Increased fecal elimination
  3. Reduced smoke-induced metabolic clearance
  4. Increased induction from nicotine withdrawal
  5. Complete cessation of renal filtration
Answer and explanation

Reduced smoke-induced metabolic clearance

Stopping tobacco smoke exposure can reduce enzyme induction and lower theophylline clearance.

Option explanations

Reduced smoke-induced metabolic clearance: Stopping tobacco smoke exposure can reduce enzyme induction and lower theophylline clearance.

Increased induction from nicotine withdrawal: The relevant induction comes from smoke exposure, not simply nicotine withdrawal.

Complete cessation of renal filtration: No renal failure is specified and this is not the key smoking interaction.

Reduced intestinal absorption: Reduced absorption would lower exposure.

Increased fecal elimination: Greater elimination would not explain the rise.
